target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures report on the activity and composition of nonperforming consumer loans. D275/D276 (2023) report NPL balance ($2.7B), the $180+ days past due/write-down portion (20%), and the current-but-nonperforming portion (60%). D268 (2024) reports NPL balance ($2.6B), the $180+ days past due/write-down portion (17%), and the current-but-nonperforming portion (58%). These are the same specific financial metrics within the same Consumer Credit Portfolio section.

D277 (2023) reports the decrease in Foreclosed properties ($18M to $103M). D268 (2024) also reports the decrease in Foreclosed properties ($14M to $89M) within the same 'Nonperforming Consumer Loans, Leases and Foreclosed Properties Activity' section. Although D268 covers multiple metrics, it specifically contains the counterpart disclosure for Foreclosed Properties activity found in D277.

comparisons.peer_topic: Nonperforming assets table reference and exclusions
comparisons.peer_summary: The provided text introduces a table of consumer, excluding credit card, nonperforming assets as of December 31, 2024 and 2023. It further details that mortgage loans past due and insured by U.S. government agencies (primarily 90+ days past due) are excluded from this specific metric due to government guarantees, with values of $121 million and $182 million for 2024 and 2023 respectively.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) provide detailed disclosures on nonperforming consumer assets and the specific treatment of government-insured loans. BAC breaks down its $2.6 billion in nonperforming consumer loans by delinquency status and credit quality, noting that $1.5 billion were current but classified as nonperforming. JPM similarly provides data on consumer nonperforming assets (excluding credit cards) and explicitly excludes mortgage loans past due and insured by U.S. government agencies (primarily 90+ days past due) from this specific metric, reporting excluded amounts of $121 million for 2024. Both disclosures highlight the importance of distinguishing between technically nonperforming but current loans and those with significant past-due status, with JPM explicitly excluding the latter group from its reported nonperforming assets table.

sentences.text: During 2024, nonperforming consumer loans of $2.6 billion remained relatively unchanged.
At December 31, 2024, $459 million, or 17 percent, of nonperforming loans were 180 days or more past due and had been written down to their estimated property value less costs to sell.
In addition, at December 31, 2024, $1.5 billion, or 58 percent, of nonperforming consumer loans were current and classified as nonperforming loans in accordance with applicable policies.
The following table presents information as of December 31, 2024 and 2023, about consumer, excluding credit card, nonperforming assets.
(a)Excludes mortgage loans past due and insured by U.S. government agencies, which are primarily 90 or more days past due.
At December 31, 2024 and 2023, mortgage loans 90 or more days past due and insured by U.S. government agencies were $121 million and $182 million, respectively.
